name: Solid silicone gluteal implants

card.summary: Surgically placed solid silicone prostheses that add permanent projection and volume to the buttocks, an option for people with little fat to transfer.
card.note: A 2019 meta-analysis reported the highest complication rate among buttock augmentation methods.

quick.overview:
Solid silicone gluteal implants are shaped prostheses placed through an incision near the tailbone, usually under or within the gluteal muscle, to enlarge and reshape the buttocks. They add volume independent of body fat.

They are described as best suited to people with little fat in the lower trunk, buttocks and thighs, who cannot supply enough tissue for fat transfer (the Brazilian butt lift). Reviews report a higher complication rate than fat grafting.
quick.how: The procedure takes about two hours under sedation, general or local anesthesia, with an incision of roughly 5 to 8 cm. Recovery is commonly four to six weeks, with full healing over several months.
quick.risks: Reported complications include infection, wound opening exposing the implant, rupture, fluid collection (seroma), capsular contracture, asymmetry, implant shifting and sciatic nerve injury. A 2019 meta-analysis of 46 publications found a 31 percent complication rate for implants against 7 percent for fat grafting.

lead: Solid silicone gluteal implants are prostheses inserted to increase the size and projection of the buttocks. Surgeons place one under each gluteus maximus muscle through a midline incision of about 5 to 8 cm over the tailbone [1].

In appearance terms, they provide fullness and shape that does not depend on the patient's own fat, which is why they are described as best for people with few fat stores in the lower trunk, buttocks and thighs [1]. The alternative is fat transfer, popularly called the Brazilian butt lift, which uses the patient's own fat but may need repeat sessions because some resorbs [1].
The literature reports more complications with implants than with fat grafting: a 2019 meta-analysis of 46 publications found a 31 percent rate against 7 percent [1].

chain: Solid silicone implant placed behind or in the gluteal muscle
Adds volume and projection regardless of body fat
angle.text: The implant itself supplies the added volume, so the result does not rely on fat availability. It is used by people who want more projection than their own tissue can provide.

paras: The surgeon makes a midline incision over the tailbone and creates a pocket for each implant under the gluteus maximus muscle. The operation takes about two hours, can be done under sedation, general or local anesthesia, and may be outpatient or overnight [1].

Fat transfer harvests fat from areas such as the abdomen, flanks or thighs and injects it into the buttocks; it avoids a foreign implant and allows return to daily activities after about two days, though some fat is resorbed and further sessions may be needed [1]. Its popularity rose in the 2010s and 2020s, largely through social media [1].

Listed risks include infection, wound dehiscence exposing the implant, rupture, seroma, capsular contracture, asymmetry, implant shifting, over-correction, sciatic nerve injury and paresthesia [1]. The overall 31 percent complication rate in the 2019 meta-analysis was the highest of the buttock augmentation methods compared [1].

A 2019 meta-analysis of 46 publications, as summarized by Wikipedia, compared complication rates among buttock augmentation techniques, finding 31 percent for implants and 7 percent for fat grafting [1].

timeline.event: Brazilian surgeon Ivo Pitanguy pioneers buttock surgery [1].
Eduardo Krulig coins the term lipoinjection [1].
